name: Fritz Haber
summary: German chemist who developed the Haber-Bosch process for ammonia synthesis and pioneered chemical warfare in World War I.

name: Clara Immerwahr
summary: German chemist and Fritz Haber's first wife, known for her suicide in protest of his chemical weapons work.

name: University of Heidelberg
summary: German university where Fritz Haber studied.

name: University of Berlin
summary: German university where Fritz Haber studied and later lectured.

name: Technische Hochschule Karlsruhe
summary: German technical university where Fritz Haber lectured and conducted early ammonia synthesis work.

aliases: Institute for Physical Chemistry and Electrochemistry
name: Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physical Chemistry and Electrochemistry
summary: Research institute directed by Fritz Haber from 1911.

name: BASF
summary: German chemical company that collaborated with Haber on industrial-scale ammonia production.

name: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1918
summary: Nobel Prize awarded to Fritz Haber for ammonia synthesis.

name: Breslau
summary: City in Lower Silesia where Fritz Haber was born.

name: Basel
summary: Swiss city where Fritz Haber died in exile.

name: Ypres
summary: Belgian town where the first chlorine gas attack was directed by Haber.

name: Germany
summary: Country where Fritz Haber lived and worked for most of his life.

name: Ammonia Synthesis
summary: Chemical process for synthesizing ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen developed by Haber.

name: Chlorine Gas
summary: Chemical weapon pioneered by Haber for use in World War I.

name: Zyklon B
summary: Insecticide later used in extermination camps, development of which Haber was later involved in.

name: Max Planck
summary: German physicist and Nobel Prize winner who spoke at Haber's memorial service.

name: Robert Le Rossignol
summary: English scientist who collaborated with Haber on ammonia synthesis.

name: Bosch
summary: German chemist and industrialist who collaborated with Haber on ammonia synthesis.
